stem: For the function $n(x)=\frac{x-1}{x^2-9}$, mark every value of $x$ that must be excluded from the domain.
solution: Only the denominator can make the fraction undefined, so solve $x^2-9=0$.
$x=1$ makes the numerator zero, so $n(1)=0$ is defined and 1 stays in the domain.
notes: Here the numerator zero 1 is a tempting extra mark, so extra-values is listed first. Marking only 3 fires missed-values (one root only), a named alternative. Marking only 1 may fire neither cleanly and is not separately mapped.
